evidence_items.concise_factual_claim: The MSc Computer Science indicative study duration is 24 months.
The programme carries 180 credits.
Global Trends in Computer Science is a 15-credit, eight-week module.
Machine Learning in Practice, Reasoning and Intelligent Systems, and Robotics appear in one elective choice group.
The final Computer Science Capstone Project is worth 60 credits and lasts 32 weeks.
A study break or reassessment can prevent completion within the indicative 24 months.
The indicative duration is 24 months, while the maximum completion period is 72 months.
evidence_items.notes: Requires the headline duration and the separate maximum-period note.

evidence_items.concise_factual_claim: An admissions appeal is a formal request to reconsider an application decision.
A complaint expresses dissatisfaction with admissions procedures, implementation, actions, or inaction.
The procedure cannot be used merely to dispute admissions staff's academic or professional judgement.
evidence_keywords_or_phrases: may not make an Appeal or Complaint

evidence_items.concise_factual_claim: A third party may submit an appeal or complaint only with the applicant's explicit written consent.
Anonymous complaints are not handled under this procedure.
Applicants should normally appeal within one month of the application decision.
evidence_keywords_or_phrases: make an appeal within one month

evidence_items.concise_factual_claim: The formal appeal review normally aims for a response within fifteen working days after receipt and acknowledgement.
The Executive Pro-Vice-Chancellor acknowledges an escalated complaint within ten working days and appoints investigators with no material interest.
A normal appeal should be made within one month, while the later Executive Pro-Vice-Chancellor stage has a ten-working-day acknowledgement target.
evidence_items.notes: Combines deadlines from different stages of the procedure.

evidence_items.concise_factual_claim: The policy distinguishes four academic-integrity categories with increasing levels of dishonesty.
A student with an unresolved academic-integrity matter cannot graduate, including while an appeal is registered.
evidence_keywords_or_phrases: No student with an unresolved academic integrity matter

evidence_items.concise_factual_claim: Personal Extenuating Circumstances are not accepted as a reason for committing academic misconduct.
Poor academic practice can include poor paraphrasing or inadequate referencing.
Collusion involves conscious collaboration on work later submitted as individual work without official approval.
Commissioned or procured work includes asking a third party to prepare all or part of an assignment, paid or unpaid.
Acceptable proofreading identifies presentation errors; adding, rewriting, or fact-checking content is unacceptable.
Submitting GAI-generated assessment work contrary to assignment guidance is treated as dishonest practice.
Category 2–4 decisions may be appealed only on procedural-error grounds in the investigation.
The policy defines escalating integrity categories, while appeals against Category 2–4 decisions are limited to procedural-error grounds.
evidence_items.notes: The category definitions and appeal restriction are separated by several pages.

evidence_items.concise_factual_claim: The coding standard aims to make assignment and project code more readable and easier to follow.
Variable and attribute identifiers should be meaningful, start lowercase, and use camel case.
Class identifiers start uppercase and should be nouns.
Constant identifiers are normally uppercase with underscores between words.
Method names start lowercase, use camel case, and should be verbs.
Comments should explain a code section's intention and outline its algorithm.
Public methods should be commented, including input variables and returned values.
Online or textbook code ideas and fragments must be precisely referenced in comments.
Variables use lowercase-leading camel case, classes begin uppercase, and constants are normally uppercase with underscores.
evidence_items.notes: Combines separate identifier rules rather than treating one naming rule as sufficient.
